title: Prek Lavea villagers protest over a land dispute
location: Prek Lavea village, Ksach Kandal district, Kandal province
scope: local village protest; reported attendance and state-directed demand are unknown
participants_original: Not reported. The article says villagers from Prek Lavea burned tires during a protest; ten families are parties to the underlying dispute, not a turnout figure.
threshold_50_evidence: Unresolved. The article gives no number of protesters; ten families are dispute parties and the “dozens” mentioned are police officers, not protesters.

start_date.summary: The article describes the protest as occurring Tuesday and dates its caption to 16 February 2021.

end_date.summary: The source gives no physical end or later closure.

location.summary: Prek Lavea village, Ksach Kandal district, Kandal province.

scope.summary: Villagers burned tires in protest over a land dispute involving ten families and private landholder Hang Raing; size and organizer are not reported.

demands.summary: The article describes the land dispute but does not state an explicit demand made to the government during the 16 February protest; state target remains unresolved.

participants.summary: Turnout is not stated. Ten families refer to parties to the dispute, and dozens refers to police.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No protester count is reported; the 50-person threshold cannot be assessed.

protester_violence.summary: The article reports villagers burning tires during the protest and describes the incident as turning violent; this records the reported property-burning act.

state_response.summary: CamboJA reports police cracked down on the protest and arrested 11 people. A separate follow-on statement alleges police violence against older people, but the exact relation to this action is unclear; other response variables remain unknown.

notes: The report describes an underlying land dispute with a private party and prior local-authority handling, but does not establish a government-directed demand at the 16 February gathering. The 11 arrests are reported as protest-related; they are not attendance. Do not use the ten dispute families or police presence as protester turnout.
open_questions: Was the gathering at least 50 people?
Did participants make a specific demand to government or local authorities, rather than to the private landholder?
Does the reported police-violence allegation refer to this gathering or only to the separate follow-on protest?
What was the gathering’s physical end?

title: Land-dispute communities hold solidarity gatherings for release of six activists
location: Separate community locations across 11 Cambodian provinces; the article names community representation from Kampong Speu, Tboung Khmum and Sihanoukville but does not enumerate all sites.
scope: Same-day, multi-sited solidarity campaign; local assemblies are described separately by location.
participants_original: RFA reports 10–20 people at each of 11 locations; it does not report a single campaign-wide count or unique participant total.
threshold_50_evidence: Each reported local gathering had 10–20 people, below 50. The 11 sites are described as a same-day campaign, but local assembly ownership and aggregation remain unresolved; do not sum sites into one ≥50 local gathering.

start_date.summary: RFA dates the local solidarity gatherings to Tuesday 23 February 2021.

end_date.summary: The article says the campaign would proceed step by step but supplies no physical end date or later completion evidence.

location.summary: The article reports separate community gatherings across 11 provinces and names representatives from some of the affected areas; it does not list every site.

scope.summary: RFA frames same-day actions in respective communities as one solidarity campaign, with banners and planned petitions.

organizer.summary: No named campaign organizer is stated; a CCFC president is quoted but not identified as organizer.

demands.summary: Banners sought dropping charges against six land activists; speakers also asked the government to resolve local land disputes and end security-force intimidation and arrests.

participants.summary: RFA reports 10–20 people at each of 11 locations. It does not supply a campaign-wide unique count; per-site ranges are retained.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Each local gathering is reported below 50. Whether the multi-sited campaign is one MM event or separate local actions requires review; no aggregate attendance is assigned.

protester_violence.summary: No event-day violence information is reported; unknown.

state_response.summary: RFA says it could not reach government spokespeople for comment. This is not coded as ignore. Prior activist arrests are separate events; all seven event-response values remain unknown.

notes: The reported campaign sought release of six land activists, resolution of local land disputes and an end to intimidation/arrests. Keep the published 10–20-person range at each location; do not convert it into a campaign-wide turnout for a local event. Article coverage comes through one RFA Khmer Service reporting chain translated into English.
open_questions: Should the same-day campaign be one coordinated event or separate community assemblies?
Can the per-site 10–20 counts be treated as distinct attendance for any national-campaign threshold?
Were planned petitions submitted and what response followed?
Did the campaign physically end on 23 February or continue through later actions?
Is there independent contemporaneous reporting beyond RFA’s English translation?
